summary: Saturday policy check and demand scan for the geography channel: added 4 topics from this week's 'redraw the whole world' breakouts (language borders, every empire at once, a new island, how Spain was assembled) and one new story shape.
why: The new market scan (27 Nov) shows small channels getting 104-151x their subscribers on world-redraw what-ifs. The language, island and empire topics score 8.1-8.25, above all but five open topics. No new policy change this month; the Feb 2027 monetisation bar is now confirmed by several outlets, so it goes to the owner as info.

findings.title: What If Borders Were Drawn by Language: 421K on 2.8K subs (149x)
findings.detail: Added as a what_if_world topic with Ethnologue's 7,170 languages and Papua New Guinea's 840; also the reference for the new 'recolour' shape.

findings.title: A new island that grows every day: 445K on 2.95K subs (151x)
findings.detail: Told as the true story of Surtsey (1963), which French journalists jokingly claimed before Iceland did.

findings.title: Every empire at the same time: 354K on 2.8K subs (125x)
findings.detail: Added with the British, Mongol, Russian and Roman peak areas from Taagepera and Turchin.

findings.title: Borders drawn by religion: 868K, but not for us
findings.detail: It would draw disputed regions by faith, which the channel profile rules out.

findings.title: YouTube's monetisation bar doubles for new channels from 1 Feb 2027
findings.detail: 8,000 watch hours or 20M Shorts views in 90 days. Sent to the owner as info; nothing in the pipeline changes.

changes.title: 4 topics added to the feed
changes.detail: 3 what_if_world and 1 why_shaped, all global and evergreen, with sourced fixed figures.

changes.title: New trial story shape 'the-recolour'
changes.detail: Wipe the borders, redraw the world by one rule, then push in where the rule does the strangest thing.
